thread:
maria: quick async standup — API GW / routing / auth / rate limits

maria: ✅ what I did yesterday: landed routing change to prefer sticky-route when cookie present; added small e2e that simulates short bursts; opened PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1289

maria: 🚧 blocker: still seeing intermittent 429s from dedicated pool during synthetic load. can reproduce locally only when kv-cache warmup is disabled. not sure if it’s batching related or auth token churn.

maria: today: dig into kv-cache TTL + batching heuristics, add more observability around per-shard inflight tokens, and ping thomas for a quick auth rotation review.

thomas: thanks — taking a look now. initial hunch is token refresh race when a subset of clients hit expired tokens and we retry, causing burst to backend. can you paste the failing request headers or a minimal repro?

maria: repro snippet attached:

```bash
# repro script (very small)
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://stg-gw.redwood.internal/predict" &
  sleep 0.01
done
```

maria: when kv-cache warmup=false the 429s start around 20s in. with warmup=true we see steady latency and no 429s.

thomas: interesting. could be backpressure from our per-conn queue plus retries. can you add a small metric for "auth.refresh_retries" and ship to staging? I can then run a canary.

lee: i can run the canary and monitor queue depth. happy to coordinate — leaving a small window at 10:30 PT to avoid noisy CI.

anya: flagged the PR for review, left a couple of nits about test flakiness. also, FYI, noticed a config typo in the ratepolicy that might cause misrouting for cookie-less flows — opened an issue #324.

maria: noted, thanks @anya. I'll fix test nits and the ratepolicy typo in a follow-up commit.

deploy-bot: canary deployed to staging (gw-canary-1289) — health checks: OK, latency p50 42ms, p95 210ms.

lee: kicking off canary load now (small burst). will post quick summary in ~10m.

thomas: also, maria — can you add a short comment in the PR about why warmup=true is the safer default for dedicated pools? helps ops when debugging later.

maria: will do. adding comment + metric change, pushing in ~1h.

lee: canary results: small burst induced ~3% 429s at ~18s, correlates with auth.refresh_retries spiking from 0->12. when i re-ran with warmup=true spike vanished. logs show concurrent refresh attempts for same user token id.

maria: great data — i'll implement a singleflight for token refresh (debounce per-token-id) and add metrics + circuit-breaker for retries.

anya: sounds good. after the singleflight + metric is in we should schedule a quick weave deploy to dedicated pool next week.

maria: thanks team — ping me if you want to pair. tagging owners: @thomas @lee. :thumbsup:
